<< I wish Steam had a [b]NEUTRAL[/b] rating. >> TLDR: Upvote as a fun roguelike. Downvote as a pool game. It is a billiards game with roguelike mechanics (think Balatro). But billiards is not just the literal table and balls. Lining up shots is as important to the game as anything else and Drop Pockets is unable to deliver on that account. If you just want a nice roguelike game, you WILL have fun with this. But if you were hoping for a great pool game with some roguelike elements, then this isn't it. Details: Incredibly amusing game where you plot out the random upgrades you get for fun builds. The kinds of builds and variety of balls in the game makes for lots of hours of interesting play. The graphics are a little on the rough and loud side, like something out of the heyday era of Flash games. It is an acquired taste. I'm not a fan of the visuals, but that's subjective. Overall, its fun enough to play around with on a very casual level. If you like playing pool, as in you really like a good simulation of the game, then just know that Drop Pockets has horrible pool mechanics. You can't even choose which part of the cue ball to hit. If you're planning to bank of the rail, forget it. That mechanic and so many basic others (aiming, motion, etc...) are not present at all. Aside from pretty much straightforward shots, you can consider ball movement as RNG. Even some simple shots are impossible since the moment you try to hot the left or right side of a ball with your cue ball, the movement becomes erratic.

A cool idea with a bit of a sloppy execution. Worth a buy, but it's no Balatro (which is not really a fair bar, Balatro might be a perfect game) The concept is really cool. Billiards, but the pockets and balls can have different attributes that can mutate the game quite a bit. Also each level has a pool shark which manipulates the table further for each game. Pretty straightforward, however, there's not a whole lot of synergy or emergent interaction between things. There's SOME, but it really doesn't come up enough. Just straight 1-to-1 interactions (shoot a Planet ball into a pocket that gives more points for planets... there's not much cross interaction between the ball types beyond that) I don't really get a lot of opportunities to build synergies that I can see, but maybe I need to unlock more. Also this game has a difficulty slider which I absolutely hate for checking off challenges. What the hell is the diff between 1.2 and 1.3? Why do we need to make this granular? If you like to fully conquer your roguelikes this will put a bad taste in your mouth. The art style is a little rough and I'm not a fan of it. It can be hard to tell what kind of ball you have at a glance unless you click on it. Also, the pool sharks are all gooner coded, if that means anything. Like, you can tell the artist WANTS to draw porn, and is used to drawing lewd women, but is toning it down for this. If it's not a hot woman, the proportions are all off and weird. Most characters are a reference to something else, which feels like wasted potential. You could have a cast of interesting original characters, but most are just ads for other games, references to youtubers, or ads for an artist. Blech. Cmon make some cool pool sharks. But it's not doing it in a way that seems like it's *supposed* to be sex appeal. It's odd. I don't like it. If it were up to me, I'd dispense with the characters entirely and make each level a special pool hall, bar, or other setting that fits the theme. Like, Iron/Space balls? Cool, that's on a space station that breaks down spaceships for scrap, and the special challenge is that the table is covered in metal debris and oil slicks. That's way more interesting than 'boob lady'. The UI is okay but lacking that dopamine juicing bing bong bells and whistles that would get you excited. The first time you max out on your multiplier you might not even notice because not much changes sound wise.

Neat idea and loads of potential, but as it stands right now I have put in my refund request and can't recommend it. I had at least 4 runs within an hour that ended up in a faulty state. Stuff like the ball somehow ending up outside the play area and no longer interacting with anything, the game not changing states when it should switch over to the boss/shark, or the cue ball re-spawning over a pocket after a scratch... over and over until the fail state was reached. It's early access, I understand that bugs are to be expected and I would gladly work around those, but when they are game stopping/ending and it happens multiple times in an hour it's frustrating... so back on the wishlist this goes. I gladly come back when it had more time in the oven.

So, I have some thoughts. I really like some aspects of this game. Different ball materials, the ability to upgrade certain balls you are more likely to want to sink, upgrading pockets, stacking (more on this), etc. These are a few things that I really like and could see being really fun and interactive with a tad more polishing in other areas that kill this game right now for me. Here are my notes on my 2 hrs I've played so far (and will likely stop there until changes have been made). Stacking - it seems that the mult stacking goes away COMPLETELY when you do a stall. Maybe I'm tripping but that's what I was noticing and I don't feel that's fair. Sometimes you are completely out of options and HAVE to stall which then punishes you greatly by completely removing the multipliers you've built up by sinking balls consecutively. I feel it would be more fair and enjoyable to remove maybe 1 stack or 2 at most and just leave it there, especially when there are instances that I've had to stall multiple times in a row to get to a ball that will get me the points I need. 1 stack per stall seems a lot more balanced because as of now the incentive is to not use stalls whatsoever despite having several of them available as a potential resource. Aiming - I'm noticing that the aiming does not line up with where you're hitting the ball. Coming from somebody who's put countless hours into 8 Ball Pool and who also plays pool irl, you need to fix this yesterday lol. Not only is the aim slightly off, but WHY OH WHY would you make the shot RNG the more off centered you are on contact. I do no understand this whatsoever. The punishment typically is that you have to hit the cue ball harder which could end up putting you in a bad spot, so it's already balanced as is. This is just normal billiards/8 ball stuff. Please fix this. Cue ball stuff - You can't move the cue ball at all on break (?) or upon scratching. LAME. You get punished for scratching already via losing turns of some sort or money, so wouldn't it make sense to be able to use this as a tactical tool? Scratch on purpose to be able to put your cue ball in a spot where you can make some stuff happen? Idk, maybe that's just me. Other thing that is a MUST is that you need to add spin control to shots. That's a big part of pool, so not having that available makes this feel a lot less like a pool game and more like something else entirely. Side note, but also very important is to change the way you add power to the ball. Maybe just a typical slider style like on 8 ball pool would be just what this needs. You have 2 different buttons right now (one to lock aim position and one to start power meter for shot) when you could literally just make it one that locks while you're sliding the cue for power (like 8 Ball Pool lol). Shop - I noticed in the shop that when you're buying a ball modifier(s) you are not able to look at a detailed view of what your balls currently have for buffs. you can see all the icons, sure, but for somebody new that's useless. it's only detrimental to not have a feature like this to be able to look before you're throwing that new buff on a ball that maybe would have made more sense on a different one. I think these are my main gripes at the moment other than the large balls are extremely annoying and I'm not sure why you'd want them on the table congesting everything and getting in the way of pockets that you very much need lol, but that's situational and nobody is forcing me to use the large balls. maybe add a hotkey to view your entire inventory a little easier too. that's not a huge deal though. All-in-all I can't honestly recommend this game to anyone in its current state despite how much I'd love to. My advice would be to take a good look at 8 ball pool to see how it's operating on a game play level. There's a reason that game is and has been one of best pool titles to ever do it (if not just the best). If you made this game feel very similar to that one as far as game play mechanics and quality of life optimizations but then, of course, kept the roguelite additives.....you will be COOKING up a good game that myself and loads of others (I'm sure of it) will be heavily addicted to. Maybe add a multiplayer option as well sometime in the future, but fix the base game first haha. I believe in you, dev(s)!! I am dying to love this game and hope you can make it happen! UPDATE for end of 2025 I have booted the game up after the major update to see what's up, but simply cannot bring myself to play because of 1 single thing that hasn't been tweaked or fixed. The rng aspect to shooting. It's not a good feel, and it's not billiards. I refuse to play this game until more realistic physics are added. It's just not fun. Still a no recommend from me :(

The physics and geometry in this pool game are way off. Frequently the shadow ball and the arrow disagree with each other by more than 5 degrees. I wish I could turn the arrow off becuase it seems to be more inaccurate. The ball-to-ball physics is way off too. With normal balls, glancing the cue ball off an object ball will send the object ball off in a direction like it was struck at no angle. I'm disappointed that this aspect of the game isn't better. After all, if you are going to play with the physics of the game as a mechanic, it better be accurate to begin with. It's like trying to cook a particular dish without a recipe and not knowing how to cook, but it's ok because you ate it a couple times before.

I love indie games and I understand that this is a work in progress. I'd really like to leave a positive review for this game because I can see the potential it has to be fun. But in its current form. it's a roguelike that dangles fun builds and mechanics in front of you and locks them behind RNG. It's incredibly difficult to get any sort of good build going when you have to play a plinko mini game to maybe get your upgrades after every round then hope to get lucky in the store before choosing your next matchup. There are a lot of different ball effects and not all of them are desirable (i.e, large balls and glass balls) but the amount of variety is the very thing that almost ensures that you won't get a build that works for the final few levels of each run. The pool mechanics are a little too basic for my taste and I kind of wish that there were things like ballspin mechanics to help you position your next shot or bonuses for combo shots or bank shots. Lastly, there's no pool table that doesn't favor either stripes or solids so when you're playing a stripe table it feels a bit like a slap in the face when you're only getting bosses and shop items that give solid upgrades. Again, this has the potential to be a really fun game but I just can't see myself returning to it if winning is more of a roll of the dice than a reward for good decision making.

I was pretty hesitant to pick this game up because there has been speculation the dev doesn't update it enough. I have to say, ever since I picked this up I am unable to put it down. I still have not won a single Run but I am getting very close, and learning the deeper strategies. I really think that this game has a huge potential to become something I would up there with Balatro, Brotato, Lone Tower, Slay the Spire in many ways - Games you can't help but keep playing and trying to end up doing everything in. There is a strong need for more improved balancing, additional content, and maybe a little more polish but this game is a gem for sure. To the dev, I truly appreciate what you have made here and hope to see it completed and much more coming!
